title: Map game weaknesses to benchmark categories instead of grinding generic game playlists
summary: Benchmark categories become more useful when they are tied to a real in-game weakness like reading or acceleration handling, instead of being treated as abstract rank ladders or random game-tagged playlists.
why: The benchmark category is useful when it points at a real game weakness, not when it is played for its own title or label alone.
This keeps scenario choice tied to a practical transfer goal instead of generic benchmark grinding.
actions: Write the in-game weakness first, then map it to the benchmark category that trains that response.
If your game problem is reading or acceleration handling, choose the benchmark category for that problem instead of a generic game playlist.
Review whether each playlist scenario serves a defined weakness or is only there because it sounds game-specific.
avoid: Do not play a game-tagged benchmark playlist just because the game name matches your main title.

drills.label: Weakness-to-category mapping
drills.reason: Mapping a real weakness to a category makes benchmark use far more actionable.

evidence.claim: Benchmark categories should be selected by attaching them to a real game weakness rather than by generic game labeling.
evidence.excerpt: Identify weaknesses in your game and attach them to one of the categories.
